name: Investments and Economics Practice Questions
description: Original practice questions on bonds, options, portfolio theory and economics (authored from public textbook concepts, not a vendor bank).

cards.prompt: When market interest rates rise, the price of an existing fixed-rate bond generally:
cards.explanation: Bond prices and yields move inversely: a fixed coupon becomes less attractive when new bonds pay more.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A bond with a $1,000 par value and a 5% coupon is trading at $950. Its current yield is closest to:
cards.explanation: Current yield = annual interest / price = $50 / $950 = 5.26%.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A bond selling at a discount has a yield to maturity that is:
cards.explanation: At a discount, YTM > current yield > coupon rate. At a premium, YTM < current yield < coupon rate.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which bond is most sensitive to a change in interest rates?
cards.explanation: Duration (price sensitivity) is higher for longer maturities and lower coupons (zero-coupon bonds have the greatest sensitivity).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Duration of 5 means a bond's price changes by approximately what for a 1% change in yields?
cards.explanation: Modified duration estimates percentage price change per 1% (100 bp) yield change, inversely.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which risk is most associated with long-term bonds when inflation rises?
cards.explanation: Inflation erodes the real value of fixed payments, so purchasing power (inflation) risk is greater on long fixed-rate bonds.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) adjust which of the following with CPI?
cards.explanation: TIPS principal adjusts with CPI; the fixed coupon rate is applied to the adjusted principal, so interest rises or falls with it.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: General obligation municipal bonds are backed by:

options: The taxing power of the issuer

cards.explanation: GO bonds rely on the issuer's taxing power; revenue bonds rely on project revenues.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An investor in the 30% federal tax bracket compares a 4% tax-free municipal bond to a taxable bond. The taxable-equivalent yield is closest to:
cards.explanation: Taxable-equivalent yield = tax-free yield / (1 - tax rate) = 4% / 0.70 = 5.71%.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An inverted yield curve means:

options: Short-term yields are higher than long-term yields
Long-term yields are much higher than short-term yields

cards.explanation: An inverted curve has short-term rates above long-term rates and has often preceded recessions.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which tool of monetary policy involves buying and selling Treasury securities?
cards.explanation: Open market operations are the Federal Reserve's primary tool; buying securities adds reserves and lowers rates.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Fiscal policy is set by:
cards.explanation: Fiscal policy is taxation and government spending, decided by Congress and the President. Monetary policy is the Fed's.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which of the following is a leading economic indicator?
cards.explanation: Leading indicators (stock prices, building permits, new orders, yield spread) turn before the economy. Unemployment is lagging, CPI lagging, and GDP is coincident.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Stagflation refers to:

options: Stagnant growth with high inflation and unemployment

cards.explanation: Stagflation combines slow growth, high unemployment and high inflation.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Gross Domestic Product measures:

options: Total value of goods and services produced within a country in a period

cards.explanation: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: If the dollar strengthens against foreign currencies, US exports generally become:
cards.explanation: A stronger dollar raises the foreign-currency price of US goods, which tends to reduce exports.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Systematic risk can be reduced by:

options: Hedging or changing asset allocation; it cannot be diversified away
Buying more stocks of the same industry

cards.explanation: Systematic (market) risk affects all securities and is not diversifiable; unsystematic risk is reduced through diversification.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Beta measures a security's:
cards.explanation: Beta measures systematic risk relative to the market; the market has a beta of 1.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A stock has a beta of 1.5. If the market rises 10%, the stock is expected to rise about:
cards.explanation: Expected move = beta × market move = 1.5 × 10% = 15%.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Under CAPM, the expected return equals:
cards.explanation: CAPM: E(R) = Rf + β(E(Rm) - Rf). With Rf 3%, beta 1.2 and market return 8%: 3 + 1.2×5 = 9%.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: The Sharpe ratio measures:

options: Return per unit of systematic risk
Excess return per unit of total risk (standard deviation)

cards.explanation: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) / σp. Treynor uses beta instead of standard deviation.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: The Treynor ratio uses which risk measure in its denominator?
cards.explanation: Treynor = (Rp - Rf) / β.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Alpha (Jensen's) represents:

options: Return in excess of that predicted by CAPM

cards.explanation: Positive alpha means the portfolio earned more than its risk (beta) warranted.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Two assets with a correlation of +1 provide:
cards.explanation: Diversification benefits increase as correlation falls; at -1, risk can be eliminated.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: The efficient frontier shows:

options: Portfolios with the highest return for each level of risk
A single optimal portfolio for everyone

cards.explanation: Markowitz's frontier plots the highest expected return available for each level of risk; the best point for an investor depends on risk tolerance.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A weak-form efficient market implies that:

options: Past price data cannot be used to earn excess returns
Insider information can be used to earn excess returns
No one can earn any return

cards.explanation: Weak form: prices reflect past price data (technical analysis fails). Semi-strong: all public information (fundamental analysis fails). Strong: all information including private.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An investor buys a call option at a $50 strike for a $3 premium. The breakeven at expiration is:
cards.explanation: Long call breakeven = strike + premium = $53. Maximum loss is the premium.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An investor buys a put option at a $40 strike for a $2 premium. The breakeven at expiration is:
cards.explanation: Long put breakeven = strike - premium = $38.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: The maximum loss of an investor who writes (sells) an uncovered call is:
cards.explanation: A naked call writer faces theoretically unlimited losses because the underlying price can rise without limit.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Selling a covered call on shares you own primarily:

options: Hedges against a large price drop

cards.explanation: A covered call earns the premium but forgoes gains above the strike, offering only a small cushion against declines.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A protective put:

options: Locks in a minimum selling price for stock held
Is sold by a short seller

cards.explanation: Buying a put against a long stock position sets a floor at the strike (less the premium cost).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An option is "in the money" when:

options: A call's strike is above the market price
A call's market price is above its strike
A put's strike is below the market price

cards.explanation: In-the-money calls have market price > strike; in-the-money puts have market price < strike.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: The two components of an option's premium are:
cards.explanation: Premium = intrinsic value + time (extrinsic) value.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Open-end mutual funds redeem shares at:

options: The market price on the exchange
NAV (net asset value) computed after the market close
The offering price at the time of the order

cards.explanation: Mutual funds forward-price at the next computed NAV; closed-end funds trade on exchanges at market prices (premium or discount to NAV).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A 12b-1 fee in a mutual fund pays for:

options: Distribution and marketing and shareholder services

cards.explanation: 12b-1 fees are included in the fund's annual expenses; the SEC/FINRA caps asset-based sales charges.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which share class of a mutual fund typically charges an upfront sales load?
cards.explanation: Class A shares have a front-end load (with breakpoints); Class B had a contingent deferred sales charge; Class C has a level load.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A REIT must distribute at least what share of taxable income to maintain its tax status?
cards.explanation: REITs must distribute at least 90% of taxable income to shareholders, among other qualification tests.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: The wash sale rule disallows a loss if the investor buys a substantially identical security within:

options: 30 days before or after the sale

cards.explanation: The 61-day window (30 days before through 30 days after) applies; the disallowed loss adds to the replacement shares' basis.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A security held for more than how long qualifies for long-term capital gains treatment?
cards.explanation: More than one year of holding gives long-term capital gains rates; one year or less is short-term.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Beneficiaries of an inherited asset generally receive:

options: A stepped-up basis to fair market value at death

cards.explanation: IRC section 1014 gives inherited property a basis equal to date-of-death fair market value (in most cases).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Roth IRA qualified distributions require:
cards.explanation: Qualified Roth distributions are tax-free when the account has been open 5 years and the owner is 59½ or older (or disabled, deceased, or first-home exception up to $10,000).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Under SECURE 2.0, required minimum distributions from traditional IRAs begin at age:
cards.explanation: RMDs begin at 73 for those reaching 72 after 2022 (rising to 75 in 2033).
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An ERISA 404(c) plan must offer participants at least how many diversified investment options with materially different risk/return characteristics?
cards.explanation: Section 404(c) requires at least three diversified options to shift fiduciary liability to the participant.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: SIPC protects customers of failed broker-dealers up to:
cards.explanation: SIPC covers up to $500,000 per customer per capacity, of which up to $250,000 may be cash. It does not protect against market loss.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: FDIC deposit insurance covers up to:

options: $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category

cards.explanation: The standard FDIC insurance amount is $250,000 per depositor per bank per ownership category.
cards.sourceRef: CFA Institute, Investments curriculum; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments (McGraw-Hill); NASAA Series 65 content outline
